surface_mechanism_description: The growth process involves alternating supply of Ga and As species, with Ga atoms and arsenic being alternately supplied to the GaAs(100) surface. During the Ga supply period, the surface adatoms migrate, and during the As supply period, the arsenic reacts with the surface. The interruption of the arsenic supply during the Ga supply period is essential for surface migration enhancement. The growth proceeds in a layer-by-layer manner under these conditions.
evidence: The interruption of the arsenic supply to the growing GaAs surface during the period of Ga supply is essential to the surface migration enhancement of the surface adatoms. It was shown that two-dimensional GaAs islands are formed when the number of Ga atoms supplied on the growing surface is not equal to the surface site number. The AFM images show that the surface morphology of the sample grown at 470°C is rougher than that at 430°C even though these samples were grown at temperatures where the ALE mode was apparently observed. It is believed that the rougher surface shown in Fig. 5 was formed under an arsenic-deficient condition due to the desorption of chemisorbed arsenic layers at a high growth temperature during the evacuation time of AsH3 in an ALE cycle.
